title: Keyboard Manager failed to map win+space shortcut

judgment.rationale: The reporter's old configuration and two follow-ups all point to Win+Space/input-language switching or Space-key mapping, but they do not isolate whether the failure comes from Windows language-switch behavior, the chosen mapping, or Keyboard Manager.
evidence: The original report uses PowerToys 0.67.1 and says the first configured mapping sometimes fails to switch input method.
A commenter says Ctrl+PrintScreen mapped to Win+Space also failed to switch input method.
Another commenter says Space cannot be mapped in their setup and the on-screen keyboard does not highlight Space when pressed.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on a current build with Windows' own Win+Space language switch as a control, then isolate the specific source/destination mapping.

fix_assessment.rationale: The historical thread combines input-method switching and general Space-key remapping, and lacks a current minimal reproduction that identifies a shared code defect.

issue_context.summary: Several old reports associate Keyboard Manager shortcut remapping with failed Win+Space input-method switching or inability to use Space in mappings.
known_information: The original report is on PowerToys 0.67.1 and names Sogou input method 13.1.0.
The original configuration image is the basis for the statement that its first mapping intermittently fails.
A later commenter independently tried Ctrl+PrintScreen to Win+Space and saw no input-method switch.
A third report says Space is unavailable in mapping setup and is not highlighted by the on-screen keyboard.
inferences: The different reports may share a Space-key event issue, but the screenshots and versions do not establish identical mapping configuration.
Windows may reserve Win+Space for language switching independently of the remapper.
issue_context.analysis: Do not infer a parser or key-hook defect from the old reports alone. Compare native Win+Space, a non-reserved destination shortcut, and the exact remap on current stable, and keep the input-method application fixed during testing.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and both comments.
No linked fix or current test result is present.

reproduce.title: Compare native input switching and remapped shortcuts
prerequisites: A Windows profile with two configured input languages or methods.
A clean Keyboard Manager profile with only one test mapping.
steps: With Keyboard Manager disabled, confirm Windows' native Win+Space switches between configured input methods.
Enable Keyboard Manager and test the original mapping with the reported input method.
Test Ctrl+PrintScreen mapped to Win+Space, then test a non-reserved destination shortcut as a control.
Open the mapping editor and test whether Space is captured as a source key; compare with the on-screen keyboard state.
reproduce.expected_result: Native Win+Space works, and any failing remapped or Space-key path is isolated to a repeatable configuration rather than conflated with language-switch state.
